## Summary
fixes #16989

<!--
copilot:summary

### <samp>🤖 Generated by Copilot at 0619c3e</samp>

This pull request adds a new feature to webpack that allows users and plugins to control the fetch priority of dynamic imports, which can affect the performance and resource management of chunk loading. It introduces a new option `dynamicImportFetchPriority` in the webpack configuration, and a new property `fetchPriority` in the `ChunkGroup` class and the import options object. It also modifies several runtime modules and the `LoadScriptRuntimeModule` class to support the `fetchPriority` option. Additionally, it adds a `.gitattributes` file to enforce consistent line endings for JavaScript files.

## Details
Adds webpackFetchPriority to magic comments
Adds dynamicImportFetchPriorityto module.parser.javascript
Consumes that and sets ChunkGroup.options.fetchPriority
Passes ChunkGroup.options.fetchPriority down to ensure chunk and co to set the right priority on the script tag

Currently completely untested but looking for early feedback

*  Introduce a new `fetchPriority` property for `ChunkGroup` class to represent the priority of fetching a chunk group dynamically ([link](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/16991/files?diff=unified&w=0#diff-3d8c1094b9972f01c64b52217e93034969d92c01fae59dd8fb841ac97a287950R31))

*  Add a new `webpackFetchPriority` option to the import options object to allow overriding the global default value for the `fetchPriority` property for a specific dynamic import ([link](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/16991/files?diff=unified&w=0#diff-391177474567b080c642e311989bb34a9a82be71c4d65e15fc2ca97e73caaf5aR146-R162))
*  Include the `fetchPriority` option when generating the code for the `ensureChunk` function in different runtime modules (`RuntimeTemplate`, `EnsureChunkRuntimeModule`, `JsonpChunkLoadingRuntimeModule`) ([link](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/16991/files?diff=unified&w=0#diff-07626cfb7da83ee25692aef62aec9dc6a32d6f0511b00e6b342121c5a87b5c75L946-R948), [link](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/16991/files?diff=unified&w=0#diff-67c80f6901340ba0f2a77f9ab9190bff6ce58cdd5ca4995cd9485fffc26a7cc9L30-R37), [link](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/16991/files?diff=unified&w=0#diff-99b22d1932803b7795bbe843d01cdf63d32e52a247610bfd9cffb95170227cc6L138-R138), [link](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/pull/16991/files?diff=unified&w=0#diff-99b22d1932803b7795bbe843d01cdf63d32e52a247610bfd9cffb95170227cc6L190-R190))

issue_context.title: "fetchPriority" for script tags
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template or we'll close your issue -->
<!-- Before creating an issue please make sure you are using the latest version of webpack. -->
<!-- Also consider trying the webpack@beta version, maybe it's already fixed. -->

# Feature Request
Ability to set _fetchPriority_ attribute on script tags.

<!-- Please ask questions on StackOverflow or the webpack Gitter (https://gitter.im/webpack/webpack). -->
<!-- Issues which contain questions or support requests will be closed. -->

Webpack doesn't offer any way to set _fetchPriority_ attribute on script tags that are managed/added by webpack.

<!-- A great way to do this is to provide your configuration via a GitHub gist. -->
<!-- Best provide a minimal reproducible repo -->
<!-- If your issue is caused by a plugin or loader file the issue on the plugin/loader repo -->

I propose adding `output.scriptFetchPriorty` option with values `boolean = false, string: 'high' | 'low' | 'auto'`
When !== false, it is used in LoadScriptRuntimeModule to add the attribute to the script tag.

## Relevant links
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#the-script-element
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/script#browser_compatibility
comments:
My usecase requires applying it globally to every lazy loaded bundle.
If we think users will want to customize this per `import` then I think what @TheLarkInn is proposing would work quite well.
If you are onboard with this work as suggested, I think we are happy to take a PR for this. Can iterate on regular or draft PR. Either works!
@aboktor Let's use `fetchPriority`, because we have built-in CSS support and it will be useful to implement for `link` too

@aboktor i.e. I think we don't need `output.scriptFetchPriority`, we have such things for modules - https://webpack.js.org/configuration/module/#moduleparserjavascriptdynamicimportpreload, so you can specify it there, just look how it is implemented for preload/prefetch
@aboktor Yeah, so you can apply it in different places, also `/* webpackFetchPriority: "high" */` should be supported too
I'm on board with this. It still applies the "global nature" for dev experience but is customizable at the module rule level and can apply to many module types.

review_comments: @aboktor , what is the purpose of allowing a boolean at all, when setting it (and regardless of the value) will result in `"auto"`? I would think just keeping it to the three enums -- "high", "low", "auto" -- would keep it both simpler and more understandable
I believe @alexander-akait added that code. I do see that pattern followed throughout webpack though.
